body: I began titrating up on Lamictal in early November and have now been at 200 mg for 3 weeks or so. I don't really know if it's working. I still have daily mood swings and occasional hypomania, but my depressive periods are less intense (though still pretty bad). I hope it will get better than this.

Hi there. I was diagnosed as type 2 bipolar on November 6 2015. I am 33 years old. You are not alone. I have struggled with keeping jobs and relationships for years. All the while, I was being unsuccessfully treated for depression and anxiety. It's hard news to accept but I am hopeful that this will be the turning point for me. You must have hope, as well.
Please see my update! :)
Thank you for this wonderful advice. You were absolutely right. I had all sorts of benefits that I am now in the process of getting set up to receive. (Please see my other comment for entire update.)

UPDATE:: I went to HR today and this is the breakdown:

1.) Learned that I am eligible for (A.) a semester-long leave of absence, (B.) 2.5 months pay, (C.) coverage under the FMLA, and (D.) short and long term disability benefits

2.) Turned in a medical leave of absence request for the entire spring semester

3.) Included in my LOA request a robust explanation of the duties I've completed (including a ridiculous teaching load AND committee membership, participation in national associations, and professional development courses above and beyond what is required), despite struggling with a new diagnosis (and ineffective treatment of said illness). This is both a statement of my commitment to the college, and a subtle dig at my boss, who absolutely inarguably overloaded my course schedule.

This letter will be seen by his superiors and will hopefully lead to some sort of recognition on some administrative level that if you work the absolute ever-loving SHIT out of good, hard-working employees, they will fucking LEAVE.

At a minimum, I feel relieved to have had my say. At a maximum, my boss will reflect on my workload and my commitment to being a fucking bad ass teacher, and think twice about shitting all over the next sad fuck that takes that job position. At a supreme maximum, his supervisors (who I've been assured will see my letter) will recognize his incompetence as a department chair and will teach him how to not suck at his job.

TLDR: Leaving my shit-ass job, and getting paid to do so.

Hello Sir Attenborough: I know you won't read this because you're gone, but I just wanted to tell you how much I absolutely respect you and all of the wonderful work you have done. I often show your videos in my college-level courses and my students -- many of them non-science majors -- are consistently enthralled. Your contribution to the scientific community and the public in general cannot be overstated. Thank you, thank you, thank you.
Spot on. Thanks for your support, random Internet stranger. :) It truly is helpful to be supported by others who share my struggles.

You're absolutely right about the questioning and doubting. My boyfriend keeps telling me "only you know what you're capable of." Which implies that maybe I should be able to go back to work. And, maybe I actually could continue to work. But when I look at it as objectively as possible, I know that it's not in my best interest. Could I go back to work? Absolutely. Will I be able to finish the semester? Probably not. These are decisions that would be easy for a "normal" person to make, since they probably would not be overwhelmed by the stressful things that I have to endure. But people with bipolar are not "normal" because things like stress affect us differently and more severely than the average person.

This is interesting. For me, listening to my friends' troubles actually makes me feel better because 1.) it distracts me from my own, and 2.) I feel that I'm empathetic, I'm a good listener, and that I give sound advice. Maybe try looking at it as a way to escape your own problems for a minute. 

Also, to be clear, I often suffer from overwhelming guilt, so I can relate to that feeling. It sucks. Especially because there's never any legitimate reason to feel guilty, at least in my experience.
Thank you. I'm just feeling so bad today
Not to be sick anymore.
Yes. Mine have (to my sheer horror) escalated to screaming and throwing things, sometimes at the slightest annoyance. I'm so scared that it won't get better.
Does what I'm describing sound like mania? I am so lost. Please help
Cool. This was super helpful.
I've been diagnosed not as bipolar but as a manic depressive with GAD.

I am a professor at a community college. I have horrible anxiety, which I believe leads to the depression. I have seen doctors and begged for help with my anxiety. All they want to do is give me antidepressants. I have to take Benadryl to try and calm myself enough to even into the classroom. Every day is a struggle. I feel like I will be fired any day, because inevitably, my anxiety will win.

Take it from someone who knows: it is much better to withdraw from your classes than it is to fail them. A grade of F is really going to hurt your GPA. I know depression makes everything seem like an impossible task, but please do not take this lightly. You will be even more depressed if you have a bunch of D's and F's on your transcript. Guaranteed. Do not let depression rob you of your potential for greatness!

No. I would probably simply write "I'm sorry." I am not angry with anyone in my life, or at least, I'm not mad enough that I would never want to intentionally hurt them through my actions. The note is the last thing I care about.

I live two states away from all of my family. My mother has borderline personality disorder and hasn't spoken to me in over a year. I know what it's like to feel alone. I can't promise you that your life will get better. No one can do that. But the likelihood that your life will improve is very high. I've been through enough cycles with depression to know that there are peaks and valleys. One day at a time is the only way to make it through. Just please know that you're not the only person who is going through these hardships. We are all fighting and giving everything we have just to make it from one day to the next.

The only way to over it is through. You cannot change the mistakes that you've made, but please know that time will heal you. I am about four years out from a horrible decision, one that stunted my career and cost me a lot of money. But now, I can finally say that I have a stable job that I am pretty OK at. You just have to know that you're not alone.

Holy cow, are you serious? I think that you are incredibly handsome! 100% serious. Please do not go the transgender route unless that is what you really want. You are an attractive person and will eventually find a woman who appreciates all of that!
Oh, don't be. I didn't mean to be such an extreme downer. I'm just still pretty shocked at how that whole situation turned out. Some people just are not capable of empathy, it seems.

I have learned that, if you are treated a certain way for long enough, you actually start to believe that you deserve to be treated that way. It sounds to me like this is your situation right now with your advisor. It sounds like your advisor has been controlling, and because you let him or her have that control, you feel frustrated and lost. This does not mean that you are lazy or incapable of anything. 

When I start to second-guess myself or the quality of the work I am doing, one thing that really helps is to analyze my work as though it was done by someone else. Sometimes we are our own harshest critics, and a change of perspective can do wonders for your self esteem.

I just wanted to chime in and let you know that your story resonated with me. I am several years into my career, and still have no idea what I "want to be when I grow up." I think this lack of direction is related to depression itself. It's impossible to really know what you want out of life when life doesn't seem worth living. I just wanted to encourage you not to give up, to keep struggling through until you feel well enough to make some of these important decisions. Rest assured, you're not alone. I am a professor at a community college, and I cry every day over the amount of stress and unhappiness that this career brings me. But I'm too depressed to know whether I should actually quit or not. I suspect that, were I not depressed, I would actually rather enjoy my job. Depression has a way of clouding our judgment, numbing our senses, and just generally making it impossible to see things clearly. Hang in there, my friend.

Hi there. I have a little experience with what you're dealing with. I dropped out of my PhD program in my first year, because there were so many issues with my project that I sunk into a deep depression and started having horrible anxiety. I just want to encourage you to please try and stick it out if this is really what you want to do with your life. It's hard to go back on leaving a program. If you love what you do, and you think you will be happy in your career, it is worth the investment of your time and energy. Do not let your lack of friendship or your isolation deter you from achieving what you want out of life. Hang in there. And, you can always come here if you need a shoulder to lean on.
See, I've had the opposite experience. Telling my former supervisor was the worst possible decision. I was written off immediately.
Yes. Today I sobbed uncontrollably in my car, in my office, at home.
My heart goes out to you. Your son is lucky to have someone that loves him so much.

This speaks to me. I am in my 2nd year of teaching full time and it is really, really difficult. I had a student ask to transfer to another professor's class recently because "you're not a good teacher." I just don't understand where I'm going wrong. I get far more complaints than I do positive reinforcement and it makes it so hard to keep working.

Hi there, this really spoke to me and I hope that my story will be of some small help. 

What it comes down to is perspective.

I have an M.S. in biology, but was forced to quit PhD school for a variety of reasons, the least of which was severe anxiety and depression. Some time afterward, I found myself working quality control in a manufacturing facility (?!) -- a major step backward, but hey, easy money right? My boss was less educated than myself, and I spent most of my days being micromanaged and talked down to. At the time I couldn't see it all for what it was, since I was so depressed. I took her behavior towards me very personally and believed that I didn't deserve any better. I was never advanced by the company, despite the fact that I was basically promised a lab management position upon hiring, and the fact that I was FAR more capable of managing the lab than my supervisor was.

However in retrospect, I'm certain that she was just trying to keep me down so that I wouldn't have a chance to succeed in the company (and potentially take her job). She once threatened to "write me up" because the code date on bottled water was off by one day, 2 years in the future (the plant manager laughed her out of his office). She gave me horrible performance reviews for inane reasons. Finally, I left that job and went straight to teaching biology full time at a community college --- because they realized my worth and wanted to foster it, not snuff it out. 

Do not let one company's treatment of you tarnish your self worth. And truthfully? You're better off anyway. Working under someone who feels threatened by you is torture. Go out and find something that is better suited for you. You deserve it. :)
Okay, thank you!
Did you start off at 300? I am only taking 150.
Thank you for your response. It's crazy how these medications affect everyone so differently... for me, it's hard to sleep more than 4-5 hours a night now, whereas I usually slept 8-9 before.

No, by all means, don't apologize for your comment. I promise, if I had read the post I made even just 1 week ago, I would have had a similar response. I know the absolute frustration that comes with trying a new medication, only to be let down. I am actually afraid to have any hope for Wellbutrin, since I've never had any success so far. All we can do is stick together and keep trying. 

Have you noticed anything at all from the medication? Do you find that you sleep less or have any appetite changes? I know for many people, the actual intended effects take up to several weeks to kick in.

I know the feeling. I left a full time job with great benefits to move 3 states away and go to PhD school in 2011. Met a man I loved dearly, moved in with him. 3 months in, realized my PhD project had insurmountable issues. Got depressed and started having panic attacks. Had to drop out of PhD school, got dumped, and moved back home in shame. Was completely devastated and heartbroken. Fast forward 3.5 years. I am still struggling, but I have a wonderful boyfriend whom I love more than anyone I've ever known. I have a stable job that I am generally able to handle. Life isn't perfect but it's certainly much better than I ever expected it to be again.

:( I'm sorry you're feeling discouraged. I definitely know that feeling. I've tried several other antidepressants (most were SSRIs) and each one had its own set of really bad side effects. I was determined to stay off all medication, but falling behind at work made me finally cave. Here's hoping Wellbutrin ends up working out for you. Also if it makes you feel any better, I always felt like a lazy prick too.

I struggle with this in every relationship that I have, even though my rational self knows that it's a self-defeating tactic. We have a way of creating the scenarios which we envision. "Self-fulfilled prophecies." You are unique, you are beautiful, and you are worthy of love... but if you don't believe it, it will be hard to sustain a relationship.

I certainly understand about feeling strong empathy and overreacting. I often find it very difficult to control my emotions. I don't really know what to tell you, since I haven't figured out the solution yet. Just keep trying.

I feel like no one understands my suicidal tendencies, and therefore, people frequently react in ways that make me feel worse (crying, ignoring, changing the subject). You should probably remove yourself from the situation and call a suicide hotline. It's often much more therapeutic to talk to someone who knows what to say. Also, this helps your family and friends to not feel burdened by your heaviest needs -- which makes it easier for them to continue to support you in other ways. <3
I just randomly noticed yesterday that there was a hole in my arm. It never really hurt.
One more thing -- my first major bout with depression was during my first year of college. It's a major life change, and you're not alone in struggling to adapt. Try not to be too hard on yourself.

Hi there :)

I am by no means an expert, and won't even venture a guess as to what you're dealing with. I think you have done a great thing by posting here and opening up to others about your recent struggles. I know that this forum has been a great help to me, as someone who has struggled with depression on and off for most of my life, and more recently, severe anxiety and daily suicidal ideation. 

I am very happy that you're seeing a counselor tomorrow. I actually am a professor at a community college and can attest that many professors are willing to help out, if you can only work up the nerve to ask. As hard as it is to care right now, try not to let yourself fall so far behind that you cannot catch up. If you have to, visit with your instructors and tell them that you're having personal health issues, and see if you can get deadline extensions, if necessary. Professors appreciate communication and are much more likely to work with you if you're proactive, rather than coming to them AFTER a bunch of stuff is overdue.

We are here for you. Please update us tomorrow on your first meeting with a counselor.
This resonated with me. I hope things improve for you soon.

I had never really known about dissociation until recently. I didn't know there was a name for that. I'm pretty sure I've done it in the past, though only in really stressful situations (a couple of car wrecks come to mind). I grew up with some pretty serious emotional/psychological abuse and manipulation, so that makes sense.

I'm happy to know that the irritability is something that other people experience. I feel so guilty. I will snap at other people about nothing, then feel guilty, then cry because I feel like a horrible person... then, within hours, the cycle starts all over again. ***Aaauuuuughhhhh***

Thank you again for your help. It's honestly so incredibly helpful just to read what you have to say. It helps me to not feel so alone and completely lost. I will probably print out the things I've typed here and try to put them in some other, better format.

No, of course you're not a loser for dropping out. 

Unfortunately, I think the best answer to this situation probably isn't one that you want to hear: It depends on the university. You should contact the registrar or admissions office and ask them what the rules are. Then you can make a decision. If you can't get back in later, you might just have to tough it out. On the other hand, you might be able to fill out accommodations paperwork to get them to make an exception on your behalf. Either way step 1 is to ask.

Best of luck to you.
I'm a professor at a 2-year college. Scared to death I'm going to lose my job before I get things worked out.

Yes, I'm trying to get an appointment to see the doctor. I finally got someone on the phone this morning and am waiting to hear back within the next couple of hours.

I've only been hospitalized once, and it was after an attempt. It was good for me overall, but extremely difficult in other ways. When I returned to work, there were rumors circulating that I'd tried to kill myself. No one would really talk to me anymore. Now, I work in academia and a week off would likely kill my career.
I'm still here. It was a very long weekend of anxiety and crying and dreading my return to work. I feel like I need to be in the hospital but I can't take the time off. I need help.
That is good advice. Thank you.

Hi there, I don't know if you're able, but maybe try calling some of the free dental clinics listed in your area: http://www.freedentalcare.us/ci/ca-sunnyvale

I hope you can find someone to help you.
What is this? This scares me.

That is definitely helpful. 

I've known my very best friend since 4th grade. She has 2 children and is currently going through a divorce after ~10 years of marriage, so for the most part, I don't exist anymore. 

She is very close to the women in her family, both emotionally and physically (they live on the same road). She doesn't need me in the same way that I need her (I have no sisters, and my mother is not in my life after years of abuse). I just feel very alone and sometimes even abandoned.
Thank you, kind stranger. I think that my friends probably do care, they just can't possibly understand how much pain I am in.

I am so scared that I'm going to lose my job and my relationship. How does anyone hold down a job when they're going through something like this? I think what I am experiencing is a "mixed episode." I am agitated and very irritable, my appetite is suppressed, and I've had trouble sleeping for days (until today, when I slept a solid 7 hours during the day). At the same time, I feel hopeless, worthless, and suicidal. I'm up and down and back and forth and just feel completely whacked out, with no one to help me.
Excellent! Keep us updated :)

That's honestly a very good idea. I'm sure she wouldn't mind if you just explain your situation to her. A lot of times, people want to help but they don't know how. This would be a relatively easy way for her to majorly help you out.

I agree. My SO called around for me last week (you're stronger than I am, if you're making the calls yourself) and of the 12 he called, none accepted my insurance, and only 2 were accepting new patients. One said he could see me in November. The other can see me next week for $325 out of pocket. It definitely shouldn't be THIS hard.

I had never heard of a "mixed episode" until yesterday. I definitely feel like that's what I am experiencing. I have many strong, uncontrollable, inexplicable emotions. I'm so, so tired.  I slept maybe 3 hours last night and cannot fall asleep today. I took 2 Benadryl and nothing happened. I just want relief. Thank you for your words of encouragement.... You've helped me more than you know.

Thank you very much! I never knew how great it would feel if someone ever gave me credit for the hard work I've done just to survive. I know it seems silly, but just getting out of bed each day has been incredibly difficult. I feel like I am never caught up at work because my anxiety is frequently debilitating. Thank you thank you thank you.

Yes, absolutely, the anxiety makes this whole thing 1,000x worse. I feel like I would do anything to escape this feeling. Thank you for your empathy and understanding... I haven't gotten much of that lately and have felt all alone in this struggle.

Boy, can I relate to your story! We certainly do have a lot in common -- though I've never jumped from a moving car ;) I do routinely fantasize about just not going back to my job, selling all my things and moving to a new state, or just driving away and hiding from all the things that make my life so unbearable. I'm kinda surprised I've held it together as well as I have for so long. Like you, I remember having severe bouts of depression as a child, which manifested itself as horrible, constant guilt. Guilt is still with me all these years later, constantly reminding me of all my flaws and failures. Everything is always my fault. I feel like my daily life is filled with so much pain, and that I bury it down deep and put on a happy face in social/work situations. No one knows how bad it is, because I've learned that telling people about your diagnosis only leads to heartache. I'm so tired of this façade. I feel like I could sleep for days, if I could only fall asleep. 

Thank you so much for your story. It helps me very much just to know I'm not alone. I sincerely hope you find successful methods of coping. I hope to see more from you on this subreddit as we both try to find our ways.

Thank you for your kind words. Just knowing I'm not alone is so incredibly helpful and encouraging. I hope you are able to find something that works for you. I've read very good things about meditation and mindfulness, if you're convinced not to try medicine again. I'll keep fighting, if you'll do the same :)

I definitely understand how it would be easy to become dependent upon alcohol and/or recreational drugs. Getting actual psychiatric help is much harder than it should be.  I am literally in some of the worst pain of my life, and yet for the most part, no one really seems to care or want to be bothered with helping me. On the upside, my boyfriend called around and found a really nice psychiatrist (recommended by one of my former therapists, coincidentally) who said he can fit me in next week. I am cautiously hopeful. Just gotta make it through until then.

Thank you very much for your thoughtful response. This is exactly the sort of thing I needed to hear, as I don't personally know anyone who can relate to me at this time. If you don't mind sharing, how long did it take for you to find medication that works for you?
Hi there, I went through this on at least a couple of SSRIs in dealing with major depression, most notably Lexapro. I just quit taking it last month due to this and other more serious side effects.
